Karthik / Lauren — see answers below and attached artifacts. I created a CSV export of the current cookie/pixel inventory and a 1-page DPIA summary for the hosted API + console. High level notes:

- Cookie / pixel behaviour:
  - Redwood does not inject 3rd-party advertising pixels on customer sites by default. Customers typically deploy our embed or SDK and manage pixels via their GTM.
  - For customers using Redwood-hosted UI components, we load a small analytics beacon (collects page URL, anonymized client_id) only after explicit consent via the customer CMP. We support OneTrust and other CMP callbacks—consent state is passed to the frontend and we only trigger pixels when consent="marketing"/"analytics" as configured.
  - Advertising vendor integrations (e.g., Meta Pixel, LinkedIn Insight) are only included via an opt-in feature and are not active without explicit consent.

- Data collected by pixels: mostly hashed client identifiers, page path, timestamp, event type. We do not send clear-text email or customer PII in pixel payloads. See cookie inventory CSV for domain/endpoint and payload column.

- Server-side fallback: we support server-side event collection for customers who prefer server-mode integrations (recommended for advanced privacy controls). In server mode, customer-owned hosts call our API; Redwood does not set browser cookies in that flow.

- DPIA summary (attached): purpose is to provide inference as-a-service; lawful basis is performance of contract & legitimate interest for product improvement (customers can opt-out of analytics); mitigations include minimization, retention limits, hashing/pseudonymization of identifiers, access controls, and SOC2 controls.

- SCCs & subprocessors: Lauren, can you confirm final language, but we do execute SCCs with EEA customers and maintain a subprocessor list on our privacy portal.

- Retention windows: request-level logs (request_id, timestamp, model_id, anonymized client_id) retained for 90 days by default. Audit logs for admin operations retained for 365 days. We can offer custom retention via contract for enterprise.

Attachments included: redwood-cookie-inventory-20250711.csv, redwood-dpia-summary-20250711.pdf, SOC2-type2-access-instructions.txt (link to secure portal).

If we need to redact anything before sharing externally let me know; otherwise I suggest Karthik send these with the short answer summary.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole

Hi Maria — thanks for the clear list. Per below, attaching our cookie inventory CSV and a one-page DPIA summary. Quick summary up-front:

- Pixel inventory: we do not inject advertising pixels by default; the hosted UI triggers a small analytics beacon only after CMP consent. See attached CSV for domains, endpoints and payload fields.
- Consent gating: supported via OneTrust callbacks; pixels/events are gated by consent categories. We also offer server-side event ingestion for customers who prefer no browser-level cookies.
- Data minimization: pixel payloads contain hashed client identifiers and event names only; we do not transmit clear-text PII in pixel requests.
- SCCs & logs: we execute SCCs for EEA customers; request logs retained 90 days, admin/audit logs 365 days (custom terms negotiable). SOC 2 Type II available under NDA — see attached access instructions.

Attachments: redwood-cookie-inventory-20250711.csv, redwood-dpia-summary-20250711.pdf, SOC2-type2-access-instructions.txt
